facts.t: The Preamble was written last, but moved first
facts.d: Its ideas entered the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946 as the Objectives Resolution — before almost anything else. The Preamble itself was adopted at the very end, so that it would match the Constitution the Assembly had actually written.

N. A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the identity card of the Constitution. K. M. Munshi called it the political horoscope of the Indian State. Both phrases now appear in judgments and in almost every UPSC answer on the subject.

facts.t: Only one amendment has ever touched it
facts.d: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 added socialist, secular and integrity. That single edit is the reason the Preamble can be shown to be amendable — while Kesavananda ensures its objectives cannot be destroyed.

bank.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution?
bank.e: Berubari (1960) held the opposite — that it was not part of the Constitution. Kesavananda reversed that, and drew most ingredients of the basic structure from the Preamble's objectives.

bank.q: With reference to the Preamble, consider the following statements:
s: It is a source of substantive power for the legislature.
It is part of the Constitution.
It can be amended, but not so as to destroy its objectives.
bank.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Preamble is not a source of power — both Berubari and Kesavananda are clear that it confers no legislative competence.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a citizen-centric term in the Preamble?
bank.e: Republic is a state-centric term describing an elected head of state. Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity and dignity of the individual are the citizen-centric ideals.

bank.as: The Preamble is called the key to open the mind of the makers of the Constitution.
bank.rs: Courts use it to resolve ambiguity in constitutional and statutory interpretation rather than as an independent source of rights.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Justice Gajendragadkar's phrase in Berubari describes exactly this interpretive function — visible in Property Owners Association and the Electoral Bonds case.

bank.q: Match List I (Preamble ideal) with List II (its illustration):
pairs: 1. Essential Practices Doctrine and the Sabarimala question
2. President bound by the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
3. Planning Commission giving way to NITI Aayog
4. Model Code of Conduct, RTI and voter inclusivity
bank.e: Socialist maps to the shift from state-led planning to participative development; secular to the neutrality questions around religious practice; republic to the elected, advice-bound head of state; democratic to representation and responsible government.

bank.q: The words socialist, secular and integrity were inserted into the Preamble by:
bank.e: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 — the mini-Constitution — is the only amendment ever to touch the Preamble.

bank.q: Consider the following judicial uses of the Preamble:
s: Property Owners Association (2024) on what counts as a material resource of the community.
ADR v. UoI (2024) striking down electoral bonds with democracy as the touchstone.
Vishaka (1997) drawing on CEDAW to frame workplace harassment guidelines.
bank.e: All three are correct — they illustrate constitutional interpretation, statutory interpretation and the reading in of ratified international obligations respectively.

bank.q: All of the following flow from the term Sovereign EXCEPT:
o: Parliament's power to make extra-territorially applicable laws
India's independent positions on Russia–Ukraine and Israel–Palestine
The requirement that the President act on ministerial advice
bank.e: That requirement flows from the Republic and Democratic character of the polity, not from sovereignty, which concerns non-interference and the pursuit of national interest.

bank.q: Which of the following best describes the Preamble's legal status?
o: It is enforceable in courts like a Fundamental Right
It has no independent legal status but is used to derive constitutional intent
It overrides Part III in case of conflict
It is a Directive Principle of State Policy
bank.e: It is not independently enforceable, yet it has been decisive in cases from Kesavananda to the Electoral Bonds judgment because it reveals the intent behind the text.

bank.as: The 42nd Amendment shows that the Preamble is amendable.
bank.rs: Kesavananda Bharati held that the Preamble's objectives form part of the basic structure.
bank.e: Both statements are true but the Reason does not explain the Assertion — it qualifies it. The text can be amended; the objectives cannot be destroyed. Holding both together is the whole point.
